stories.title: David Jones’ total debt is over $400m including millions owed to staff, administrators confirm
summary: Creditors meeting hears upmarket retailer owes $11m to employees and recorded a net loss of $228m last financial yearGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastUpmarket retailer David Jones collapsed into administration earlier this month owing well over $400m, after accelerating financial losses and reputational damage threatened its ability to stock shelves for Christmas.About 500 creditors attended its first meeting on Tuesday, where administrators McGrathNicol broke down the 188-year-old chain’s massive debt pile, including an estimated $180m owed to suppliers and $11m to employees.

stories.title: Rio Tinto agrees to pay US$250m to begin repairing ‘devastation’ left by Panguna mine
summary: Community leader says fund gives chance to find solutions to ‘huge problems we have been living with since the days of the mine’s operation’Anglo-Australian miner Rio Tinto has agreed to pay a quarter-of-a-billion dollars to begin the clean-up of the toxic Panguna mine site it abandoned more than three decades ago.Panguna, once one of the world’s most profitable gold and copper mines, was shuttered in 1989 after violent protests over environmental damage and the inequitable division of the mine’s profits sparked a decade-long civil war on the Papua New Guinean island of Bougainville.

stories.title: Fiona the hippo under veterinary care after eating hat at Cincinnati zoo
summary: Knit hat caught in ceiling fan and flung into enclosure eaten by Fiona, who is being closely monitored by zoo staffThe Cincinnati zoo says Fiona, its beloved hippo who became a global celebrity after her premature birth nearly a decade ago, is undergoing veterinary care after swallowing a knit hat that got into her enclosure.Zoo veterinarians and staff are monitoring Fiona and working to help her pass the hat, the zoo said in a statement Monday.

stories.title: Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda
summary: Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.

stories.title: Labor policy backflip will allow more backpackers to work in regional Australia
summary: Number of people allowed to stay for third year on holidaymaker visa to be increased from 5,000 to 25,000 under revised planGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastThe federal government has backpedalled on its plan to cut backpacker numbers, arguing the change is the “best possible outcome” for regional industries who had criticised the crackdown because they rely on travellers for labour.On Tuesday, the Albanese government announced it would lift the proposed cap on third-year working holiday visas, boost regional work requirements and delay the start of a new ballot system.

stories.title: Proposed NSW laws to allow coalmine to increase production pose ‘serious corruption risk’
summary: Bill to authorise expansion at Mount Pleasant coalmine, subject to a landmark high court decision, will be debated this weekGet our daily political email, free app or daily news podcastA New South Wales government bill to increase coal production at a Hunter Valley coalmine creates a “serious corruption risk” for the state due to a clause that would give the resources minister “king-like” powers, the barrister and anti-corruption campaigner Geoffrey Watson says.The state parliament will this week debate legislation to allow MACH Energy to increase coal production at the Mount Pleasant mine in Muswellbrook by 32% to 16.5m tonnes per year.

stories.title: Band of baby sea turtles swims into ocean after historic California nesting
summary: Hatchlings emerge after discovery in September of first sea turtle nests ever to have been recorded on US west coastTwo months after the discovery of the first sea turtle nests ever to have been recorded on the US west coast, the eggs have hatched – and California’s first group of 75 native-born olive ridley sea turtles have been released into the Pacific.The eggs incubated at the Aquarium of the Pacific in Long Beach after the historic discovery of two separate nests in September at southern California beaches, a shift likely driven by this year’s El Niño conditions.
